mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate relative to its 12-month moving average signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates for equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as a predictor of 20-day returns falls below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window or average 20-day returns in easing periods are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 4.5% in the most recent monthly reading, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Average 5-day returns in months with UNRATE > 4.5% are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC for UNRATE as a 5-day predictor falls below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in residential investment (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a contraction in the housing sector, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC for RSAFS-HOUST interaction as a 20-day predictor falls below 0.03 over any 3-year window or average 20-day returns in contraction periods are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO) below its 3-month moving average, manufacturing sector slowdown reduces corporate profit growth expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Average 60-day returns during INDPRO contraction periods are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC for INDPRO as a 60-day predictor falls below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption (RSAFS) relative to its 12-month moving average indicates strong consumer spending that supports corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC for RSAFS as a 20-day predictor falls below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window or average 20-day returns in consumption growth periods are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When year-over-year CPI inflation exceeds 3.0%, it signals persistent inflation that triggers monetary policy tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Average 20-day returns in CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.0% periods are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC for CPIAUCSL as a 20-day predictor falls below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in unemployment (UNRATE) and decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a weakening labor market that reduces consumer confidence and spending, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC for UNRATE-PAYEMS interaction as a 5-day predictor falls below 0.03 over any 2-year window or average 5-day returns in deterioration periods are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In periods of rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 2.0%, monetary tightening increases borrowing costs and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Average 60-day returns during FEDFUNDS > 2.0% periods are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as a 60-day predictor falls below 0.03 over any 3-year window.
